title: Client adapter contract: resumable iterators, idempotent paging, and streaming backpressure
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Define a single, language-idiomatic contract and acceptance criteria for paginated fetches, resumable iterators, retry semantics, and streaming APIs across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. The goal is to enable zero-downtime client upgrades and predictable developer expectations when switching runtime models or server fallbacks.
background: Multiple engineering teams have implemented divergent client semantics for pagination and streaming. Differences include: cursor format (opaque token vs page index), retry idempotency markers, streaming framing and backpressure strategies, and how partial results are surfaced on error. This variability creates integration breakage during server-side rollouts, complicates feature parity, and increases SDK maintenance cost.
goals: Specify canonical cursor format and stable resume token header (X-Redwood-Resume) so servers and clients can agree on resume semantics.
Define idempotent retry behavior for page fetch and streaming chunks with clear client backoff and max-attempts defaults.
Provide language-idiomatic contracts for resumable iterators: Python async iterator, TypeScript AsyncIterable, Go iterator/Enumerator pattern.
Document compatibility policy to allow graceful degradation from streaming to buffered/polling fallback without surface-breaking changes.
Create acceptance tests and example snippets for all three languages that can be run in CI for SDKs and runtime compatibility checks.
non_goals: Mandating a single client library implementation across languages (we only standardize the contract).
Specifying transport-level wire protocol beyond high-level framing (protocol buffers vs JSON is out of scope).
requirements: R1: Pagination must expose an opaque resume_token string returned by the server; clients must treat it as an uninterpreted token and persist it for resume behavior.
R2: Clients must surface a stable cursor field in responses named resume_token. Servers must not change token semantics during minor releases without migration guidelines.
R3: Python SDK: Provide an async iterator that yields items and persists the last_seen_resume_token; iterator supports .resume(token) to start from token.
R4: TypeScript SDK: Provide AsyncIterable<T> with an optional resume(cursor?: string) factory; support for for-await-of and manual next() with cursor persistence.
R5: Go SDK: Provide an Enumerator interface with Next(ctx) (Item, resumeToken string, err error) and a Resume(ctx, token) constructor helper.

R6: Retry semantics: All paginated page fetches must be idempotent if retried; servers will accept X-Redwood-Idempotency header for page-level operations. Clients retry only idempotent reads by default; write-like endpoints excluded.

R7: Streaming: Define chunk frames that include optional resume_token annotations at chunk boundaries. Clients must expose an onPartialError handler for recoverable mid-stream errors with the last resume token.
R8: Backpressure: TypeScript/Python streaming APIs must respect consumer-driven pull (AsyncIterable/async iterator), Go must expose a context-aware Next(ctx) to allow cancellation.

R9: Compatibility: New SDK versions must accept both legacy numeric page indices (legacy_cursor) and the canonical resume_token for at least one release window; servers will return both fields when in migration mode.
R10: Telemetry: SDKs must emit structured trace metadata for pagination and streaming events (start, resume, partial_error, complete) and include resume_token in spans/tags.
R11: Timeouts & backoff: Default page fetch timeout 10s, streaming idle_timeout 30s, exponential backoff with jitter for retries; defaults configurable by client consumer.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: End-to-end test where server injects transient chunk error at mid-stream; SDK resumes from provided resume_token and yields no duplicate items.
AC2: Cross-language CI job validates that a saved resume_token from Python can resume a TypeScript stream and vice versa (interop smoke test).
AC3: SDK default retry behavior stops after 5 attempts, backing off with jitter; test asserts retries adhere to backoff schedule within tolerance.
AC4: When server returns both legacy_cursor and resume_token during migration, SDK selects resume_token and logs a migration warning but continues to work.
AC5: Streaming APIs must allow consumer cancellation: Python/TS by breaking iteration, Go by canceling context; server sees corresponding cancellation within 500ms under normal network conditions.
AC6: Telemetry events emitted for start/resume/partial_error/complete with resume_token attached; verification script validates presence in traces.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish contract PRD and example snippets to the SDK repo and notify SDK maintainers.
2) Create a small compatibility shim on server to emit both legacy_cursor and resume_token for two release cycles.
3) Implement acceptance tests in sdk-integration CI (Python/TS/Go).
4) Release SDKs with opt-in feature flag (resume_token-first) and monitor compatibility metrics.
5) Flip default after one deprecation window and remove legacy_cursor support on server afterwards.
migration_impact: Minor for clients that already rely on numeric pages; servers will provide dual fields during migration. Consumers who persist legacy numeric offsets will continue to function until servers remove legacy_cursor after the deprecation window. Ops and SDK teams must coordinate feature flagging to avoid client breakage.
compatibility_policy: Policy-1: Backwards compatible fields may be added; removal requires a deprecation window of at least 12 weeks and clear migration docs.
Policy-2: Resume tokens are opaque; servers must not encode semantic meaning that clients depend on.
Policy-3: Streaming fallbacks (server switches to polling) must maintain the same surface shape; SDKs should expose a 'mode' hint but not break existing call sites.
tradeoffs_considered: A) Opaque tokens vs structured tokens: opaque tokens maximize server flexibility but make debugging harder. We choose opaque tokens with optional debug metadata emitted in telemetry.
B) Strict unified API vs language-idiomatic APIs: we choose a contract + idiomatic surface to minimize friction for language consumers.
C) Server-driven retries vs client-driven retries: favor client-driven retries for network recoverability and to avoid accidental double-processing.
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial draft PRD shared with SDK leads (Python, TS, Go). Asked for language-specific ergonomics feedback.
2026-02-18: Feedback from TS lead (Lina Ortega): prefer factory resume() over passing token to next() for ergonomics; incorporated into TS examples.
2026-02-25: Security review flagged potential PII leakage if resume_token contains user identifiers; decided to require server-side masking and telemetry-only debug metadata.
2026-03-03: Runtime team will emit legacy_cursor for two cycles; ENG dependency ENG-2079 created to implement dual-field shim.
2026-03-10: Added AC for cross-language interop tests after SOC/QA request.
notes: Maintain clear migration docs and include copy-paste examples for quick adoption. Coordinate with Customer Success for early adopter customers who persist offsets in external stores.
